import pandas as pd

# File paths for all source CSV files
source_files = {
    "source0": "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_99/training_0.csv",
    "source1": "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_99/training_1.csv",
    "source2": "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_99/training_2.csv",
    "source3": "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_99/training_3.csv",
    "source4": "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_99/training_4.csv",
    "source5": "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_99/training_5.csv",
    "source6": "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_99/training_6.csv",
}

# Step 1: Load all source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
df0 = pd.read_csv(source_files["source0"], index_col=0)  # ['Name', 'tram km per capita', 'GWP_bustram']
df1 = pd.read_csv(source_files["source1"], index_col=0)  # ['Name', 'BUURTCODE', 'Population', 'food_consumed', 'Income per capita', 'Amount per capita']
df2 = pd.read_csv(source_files["source2"], index_col=0)  # ['Name', 'Type', 'green gas', 'nongreen gas', 'BUURTCODE']
df3 = pd.read_csv(source_files["source3"], index_col=0)  # ['Name', 'type', 'Water consumption', 'Household size', 'Average area', 'BUURTCODE']
df4 = pd.read_csv(source_files["source4"], index_col=0)  # ['Name', 'train km per capita', 'GWP_train']
df5 = pd.read_csv(source_files["source5"], index_col=0)  # ['Name', 'Type', 'green electricity', 'nongreen electricity', 'BUURTCODE']
df6 = pd.read_csv(source_files["source6"], index_col=0)  # ['Name', 'BUURTCODE', 'car km per capita', 'GWP_car']

# Step 2: Analyze keys and join strategy
# All tables have 'Name' column, and many have 'BUURTCODE' (sometimes with different casing).
# We will join on 'Name' as the primary key because it is common to all and unique in examples.
# For columns with different casing of 'type'/'Type', we will keep both as in target schema:
# Target schema has 'Type_x', 'Type_y', and 'type' (lowercase).
# From sources:
# - df2 has 'Type' (for green gas, nongreen gas)
# - df5 has 'Type' (for green electricity, nongreen electricity)
# - df3 has 'type' (lowercase) (Water consumption, Household size, Average area)
# So we will rename these accordingly to match target schema.

# Step 3: Prepare each dataframe for join by renaming columns to target schema names

# df0: ['Name', 'tram km per capita', 'GWP_bustram']
# no rename needed for these columns
df0_renamed = df0.copy()

# df1: ['Name', 'BUURTCODE', 'Population', 'food_consumed', 'Income per capita', 'Amount per capita']
# no rename needed
df1_renamed = df1.copy()

# df2: ['Name', 'Type', 'green gas', 'nongreen gas', 'BUURTCODE']
# Rename 'Type' to 'Type_y' to match target schema
df2_renamed = df2.rename(columns={"Type": "Type_y"})

# df3: ['Name', 'type', 'Water consumption', 'Household size', 'Average area', 'BUURTCODE']
# 'type' matches target 'type' (lowercase)
df3_renamed = df3.copy()

# df4: ['Name', 'train km per capita', 'GWP_train']
# no rename needed
df4_renamed = df4.copy()

# df5: ['Name', 'Type', 'green electricity', 'nongreen electricity', 'BUURTCODE']
# Rename 'Type' to 'Type_x' to match target schema
df5_renamed = df5.rename(columns={"Type": "Type_x"})

# df6: ['Name', 'BUURTCODE', 'car km per capita', 'GWP_car']
# no rename needed
df6_renamed = df6.copy()

# Step 4: Join all dataframes on 'Name'
# We will do a sequence of left joins starting from df1 (which has many key columns)
# to ensure we keep all rows from df1 (which has 56 tuples) and enrich with others.
# However, df0, df4, df6 have 111 tuples, so to not lose data, we will do outer joins on 'Name'
# to keep all data from all sources.

# Start with df1 as base (has many demographic and economic columns)
df_merged = df1_renamed

# Join df5 (green electricity) on 'Name'
df_merged = pd.merge(df_merged, df5_renamed[['Name', 'Type_x', 'green electricity', 'nongreen electricity', 'BUURTCODE']], on='Name', how='outer', suffixes=('', '_df5'))

# Join df2 (green gas) on 'Name'
df_merged = pd.merge(df_merged, df2_renamed[['Name', 'Type_y', 'green gas', 'nongreen gas', 'BUURTCODE']], on='Name', how='outer', suffixes=('', '_df2'))

# Join df3 (water consumption etc.) on 'Name'
df_merged = pd.merge(df_merged, df3_renamed[['Name', 'type', 'Water consumption', 'Household size', 'Average area', 'BUURTCODE']], on='Name', how='outer', suffixes=('', '_df3'))

# Join df6 (car km per capita) on 'Name'
df_merged = pd.merge(df_merged, df6_renamed[['Name', 'BUURTCODE', 'car km per capita', 'GWP_car']], on='Name', how='outer', suffixes=('', '_df6'))

# Join df4 (train km per capita) on 'Name'
df_merged = pd.merge(df_merged, df4_renamed[['Name', 'train km per capita', 'GWP_train']], on='Name', how='outer')

# Join df0 (tram km per capita) on 'Name'
df_merged = pd.merge(df_merged, df0_renamed[['Name', 'tram km per capita', 'GWP_bustram']], on='Name', how='outer')

# Step 5: Resolve BUURTCODE columns
# After merges, multiple BUURTCODE columns exist:
# - from df1: 'BUURTCODE'
# - from df5: 'BUURTCODE_df5'
# - from df2: 'BUURTCODE_df2'
# - from df3: 'BUURTCODE_df3'
# - from df6: 'BUURTCODE_df6'

# Target schema has:
# 'BUURTCODE_x_x', 'BUURTCODE_y_x', 'BUURTCODE', 'BUURTCODE_x_y', 'BUURTCODE_y_y'

# From target examples and source info, likely:
# - 'BUURTCODE_x_x' corresponds to df5 (green electricity) BUURTCODE
# - 'BUURTCODE_y_x' corresponds to df2 (green gas) BUURTCODE
# - 'BUURTCODE' corresponds to df1 (main demographic)
# - 'BUURTCODE_x_y' corresponds to df3 (water consumption)
# - 'BUURTCODE_y_y' corresponds to df6 (car km per capita)

# We will assign accordingly, filling missing values from available columns if needed.

df_merged['BUURTCODE_x_x'] = df_merged['BUURTCODE_df5']
df_merged['BUURTCODE_y_x'] = df_merged['BUURTCODE_df2']
df_merged['BUURTCODE'] = df_merged['BUURTCODE']  # from df1
df_merged['BUURTCODE_x_y'] = df_merged['BUURTCODE_df3']
df_merged['BUURTCODE_y_y'] = df_merged['BUURTCODE_df6']

# Step 6: Drop the intermediate BUURTCODE columns used for assignment
df_merged.drop(columns=['BUURTCODE_df5', 'BUURTCODE_df2', 'BUURTCODE_df3', 'BUURTCODE_df6'], inplace=True)

# Step 7: Ensure all target columns are present and in correct order
target_columns = [
    'Name', 'BUURTCODE_x_x', 'Population', 'food_consumed', 'Income per capita', 'Amount per capita',
    'Type_x', 'green electricity', 'nongreen electricity', 'BUURTCODE_y_x', 'Type_y', 'green gas', 'nongreen gas',
    'BUURTCODE', 'type', 'Water consumption', 'Household size', 'Average area', 'BUURTCODE_x_y', 'BUURTCODE_y_y',
    'car km per capita', 'GWP_car', 'train km per capita', 'GWP_train', 'tram km per capita', 'GWP_bustram'
]

# Some columns might be missing due to outer joins, fill them with appropriate types and NaNs
for col in target_columns:
    if col not in df_merged.columns:
        # Determine type by target schema hints:
        # string columns: 'Name', 'Type_x', 'Type_y', 'type'
        # integer columns: 'BUURTCODE_x_x', 'Population', 'Income per capita', 'BUURTCODE_y_x', 'BUURTCODE', 'BUURTCODE_x_y', 'BUURTCODE_y_y'
        # float columns: the rest
        if col in ['Name', 'Type_x', 'Type_y', 'type']:
            df_merged[col] = pd.NA
        elif col in ['BUURTCODE_x_x', 'Population', 'Income per capita', 'BUURTCODE_y_x', 'BUURTCODE', 'BUURTCODE_x_y', 'BUURTCODE_y_y']:
            df_merged[col] = pd.NA
        else:
            df_merged[col] = pd.NA

# Step 8: Reorder columns to target schema order
df_final = df_merged[target_columns]

# Step 9: Convert columns to correct dtypes as per target schema
# Target schema types:
# string: 'Name', 'Type_x', 'Type_y', 'type'
# integer: 'BUURTCODE_x_x', 'Population', 'Income per capita', 'BUURTCODE_y_x', 'BUURTCODE', 'BUURTCODE_x_y', 'BUURTCODE_y_y'
# float: all others

# Convert string columns
for col in ['Name', 'Type_x', 'Type_y', 'type']:
    df_final[col] = df_final[col].astype("string")

# Convert integer columns (allowing NA)
int_cols = ['BUURTCODE_x_x', 'Population', 'Income per capita', 'BUURTCODE_y_x', 'BUURTCODE', 'BUURTCODE_x_y', 'BUURTCODE_y_y']
for col in int_cols:
    df_final[col] = pd.to_numeric(df_final[col], errors='coerce').astype('Int64')

# Convert float columns
float_cols = [c for c in target_columns if c not in ['Name', 'Type_x', 'Type_y', 'type'] + int_cols]
for col in float_cols:
    df_final[col] = pd.to_numeric(df_final[col], errors='coerce')

# Step 10: Save the final dataframe to the target CSV file
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_99/target_multisource_cot.csv"
df_final.to_csv(output_path, index=False)
